study_identification.title: Deep Normative Tractometry for Identifying Joint White Matter Macro- and Micro-structural Abnormalities in Alzheimer's Disease

study_characteristics.study_objective: Propose Deep Normative Tractometry (DNT), a VAE-based normative model to encode joint macro- and micro-structural white matter tract profiles trained on healthy controls, and evaluate detection of along-tract abnormalities in MCI/AD with transfer learning to an independent Indian cohort and comparison to BUAN tractometry.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group-level detection of along-tract abnormalities in MCI/AD and qualitative/quantitative comparison with BUAN tractometry results; specific statistical tests or effect sizes are not described in the provided text.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: DNT detects widespread along-tract diffusivity abnormalities in MCI/AD, aligning with BUAN, and may help distinguish anisotropy-related changes from tract macrostructure.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using a VAE-based normative model trained on healthy controls and adapted via transfer learning, the study reports widespread along-tract deviations in diffusivity measures among MCI and AD participants, with patterns closely matching those detected by the BUAN tractometry pipeline. Incorporating tract geometry appears beneficial for teasing apart anisotropy vs macrostructural changes. Numerical effect sizes and region-wise statistics are not provided in the available text.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Key sample details (group sizes, demographics), preprocessing/QC specifics, and explicit deviation metrics/thresholds are not reported in the provided text, limiting assessment of robustness and generalizability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The approach includes transfer learning to adapt the normative model to a different cohort/domain and emphasizes joint modeling of tract macro- and micro-structure.
